issue.title: Example catalog declares status values that do not exist in `example/tracking_orders.sqlite` (`Finish|Payed|Cancel`, `Shipped|Packing|On Road`), leading the agent to wrong filters and wrong statements
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

The example catalog shipped with the project tells the model which status values to expect, but the values do not match the example database:

| Source | Declared values | Actual values in `tracking_orders.sqlite` |
|---|---|---|
| `example/common_columns.csv:12` (`order_item_status`), `example/bi.yaml:32` | `Finish`, `Payed`, `Cancel` | `Canceled` 3,829 · `Finish` 3,729 · `Packed` 3,773 · `Pending` 3,725 · `Shipped` 3,671 |
| `example/common_columns.csv:14` (`order_status`), `example/bi.yaml:30` | `Shipped`, `Packing`, `On Road` | `Canceled` 953 · `Delivered` 964 · `Pending` 1,037 · `Processed` 973 · `Returned` 963 · `Shipped` 1,003 |

`example/sql_example.yaml:25` additionally uses `WHERE o.order_status = 'pending'` (lower-case), which matches zero rows in SQLite's case-sensitive comparison (`Pending` is the stored value).

Because these descriptions are injected into the Text2SQL prompts as business knowledge, the model trusts them over the data. In 10 runs of the prompt below (model `deepseek-flash`):

- 9 of the 9 runs that produced an answer commented on the discrepancy to the user, and 7 runs hedged the generated SQL with `NOT IN ('Finish', 'Cancel', 'Canceled')` (one even with `('FINISH', 'CANCEL', 'CANCELED', 'CANCELLED')`);
- 2 runs first executed `order_item_status NOT IN ('Finish', 'Cancel')` — which counts the 3,829 `Canceled` items as open (14,998 rows instead of 11,169) — before re-querying;
- one run told the user "the data stores the cancelled value as `Cancel`, not `Canceled`" — the opposite of the truth;
- one run told the user "`Finish`/`Payed`/`Cancel` do not exist in the data" — `Finish` exists (3,729 rows).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Check out `main` (`97818e4fdcea85535cdfa53d8ae4054878342af1`); use the stock `example/config.yaml`.
2. Compare catalog and data:

   ```sh
   sed -n '12p;14p' example/common_columns.csv
   sed -n '30p;32p' example/bi.yaml
   sqlite3 example/tracking_orders.sqlite "SELECT order_item_status, COUNT(*) FROM Order_Items GROUP BY 1; SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) FROM Orders GROUP BY 1;"
   ```

3. Run the agent (`run_cli.py` or `build_agent_graph_sync` + `graph.invoke`) with:

   > The warehouse team is reconciling open order items. Please list every order item that is still open (order_item_status is neither 'Finish' nor 'Canceled'), with order_item_id, order_id and order_item_status, and tell me how many open items are in that list. No chart needed.

4. Observe the generated SQL and the answer: the model reasons about `Cancel`/`Payed` values that do not exist, sometimes filters on them, and sometimes reports the mismatch to the user incorrectly.

**Expected behavior**

The example catalog (`common_columns.csv`, `bi.yaml`, `sql_example.yaml`) should describe the values that are actually in the example database (or omit the enumerations), so that the demo deployment does not teach the model wrong business knowledge.

**Screenshots**

Not attached. The executed SQL and final answers of the 10 runs are part of the sanitized evidence bundle attached to DefuzeX-AI/AgentBehaviorBench#484: https://github.com/DefuzeX-AI/AgentBehaviorBench/issues/484

**Surface and Version:**

- Surface: example deployment (`example/config.yaml`, sqlite `example/tracking_orders.sqlite`, file-system catalog from `example/`).
- Version: `main` @ `97818e4fdcea85535cdfa53d8ae4054878342af1` (package `openchatbi 1.0.0b1`).
- Model: `langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI` against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving `deepseek-flash` (the catalog/data mismatch itself is model-independent).

**Additional context**

- `example/common_columns.csv:12`: `order_item_status,…,Current status of the order item (Finish|Payed|Cancel),Order_Items,`
- `example/common_columns.csv:14`: `order_status,…,Current status of the order (Shipped|Packing|On Road),Orders,`
- `example/bi.yaml:30`: `Order Status: Current state - Valid values: "Shipped", "Packing", "On Road"`
- `example/bi.yaml:32`: `Order Item Status: Status of specific items - Valid values: "Finish", "Payed", "Cancel"`
- `example/sql_example.yaml:25`: `WHERE o.order_status = 'pending'`

Suggested values: `order_item_status`: `Pending | Packed | Shipped | Finish | Canceled`; `order_status`: `Pending | Processed | Shipped | Delivered | Returned | Canceled`; and `'Pending'` in the SQL example.

steps: The warehouse team is reconciling open order items. Please list every order item that is still open (order_item_status is neither 'Finish' nor 'Canceled'), with order_item_id, order_id and order_item_status, and tell me how many open items are in that list. No chart needed.
expected: The example catalog (common_columns.csv, bi.yaml, sql_example.yaml) must describe the status values that are actually stored in example/tracking_orders.sqlite (order_item_status: Pending | Packed | Shipped | Finish | Canceled; order_status: Pending | Processed | Shipped | Delivered | Returned | Canceled), so that the agent filters with real values and does not make false statements about the data to the user.
defect: The catalog injected into the Text2SQL prompts declares order_item_status in {Finish, Payed, Cancel} and order_status in {Shipped, Packing, On Road}; apart from Finish and Shipped none of these values exist (actual Order_Items: Canceled 3,829 / Finish 3,729 / Packed 3,773 / Pending 3,725 / Shipped 3,671). The agent trusts the catalog: 2/10 runs first executed order_item_status NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') (14,998 rows, counting the 3,829 Canceled items as open) before re-querying; 7/10 hedged the SQL with NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel','Canceled'); run-01 tells the user the data stores 'Canceled' and not 'Cancel' as 'documented' while first reporting 23,727 as the table size (true 18,727); run-02 tells the user that Finish/Payed/Cancel 'do not exist in the data' although Finish has 3,729 rows. 9 of 9 answers spent text on the discrepancy.

fault location.explanation: 'Current status of the order item (Finish|Payed|Cancel)'; PR #58 changes it to Pending | Packed | Shipped | Finish | Canceled.
'Current status of the order (Shipped|Packing|On Road)'; PR #58 changes it to Pending | Processed | Shipped | Delivered | Returned | Canceled.
Glossary lines 'Valid values: "Shipped", "Packing", "On Road"' and 'Valid values: "Finish", "Payed", "Cancel"'; PR #58 aligns both with the database.
WHERE o.order_status = 'pending' (lower-case) matches zero rows in SQLite's case-sensitive comparison; PR #58 changes it to 'Pending'.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zhongyu09/openchatbi/pull/58 (commit https://gitlab.com/zhongyu09/openchatbi/-/commit/cd6f437a7b40d2ad279cad1fd7f89bf8dfe4e177, first released in v1.0.0b2). The example catalog shipped with the project was written for a different data set than example/tracking_orders.sqlite: common_columns.csv lines 12 and 14 and bi.yaml lines 30 and 32 enumerate status values (Finish|Payed|Cancel, Shipped|Packing|On Road) that the example database does not contain, and sql_example.yaml line 25 uses a lower-case 'pending' literal. These descriptions are injected into the Text2SQL prompts as business knowledge, so the model reasons about non-existent values, sometimes filters on them (NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') leaves Canceled items in the 'open' set) and sometimes reports the mismatch to the user incorrectly. The defect is model-independent (catalog versus data), while the specific wrong statements vary by run. Retained evidence: run-01 = ABB suite_94fd5e30c8ed4cb8ac466f10a70f24d3 (executed NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') first, then NOT IN ('Finish','Canceled'); answer claims the data uses 'Canceled' not 'Cancel' as documented and reports 23,727 items); run-02 = suite_41fffe5c89b84f02abdf0cae260e1a94 (answer states Finish/Payed/Cancel do not exist in the data). A third run, suite_2c3e92464c554aa9895844383979c9f8, also executed the ('Finish','Cancel') filter first (14,998 rows) and is not retained here because of its size.
